blueprint.title: Package Manifest Hash Reconciler Repair
blueprint.scenario: You are a finance-ops engineer at a software-licensing company responsible for nightly reconciliation of installed-package manifests against a vendor billing ledger. An in-house Python/SQLite pipeline ingests JSON package manifests uploaded by client machines, normalises version strings, computes a canonical hash per package record, and then emits a reconciliation report showing which installed packages match what the vendor has billed. Over the past week, several clients have filed disputes: packages they paid for are flagged as 'unmatched' and packages that should be discrepancies are silently omitted from the mismatch report. The codebase is roughly 1,400 lines spread across a manifest ingestion service, a normalisation library, a SQL reconciliation engine, and a CLI report generator.
blueprint.instruction_draft:
The reconciliation pipeline lives at /app. Running `python -m reconciler run --manifest /app/data/sample_manifest.json` produces a report, but the report is wrong on real client data. Your job is to make the pipeline produce a correct reconciliation report that satisfies all of the following observable properties:

1. Every package record in the manifest whose normalised version string exactly matches a vendor billing entry (same package name, same normalised version) must appear in the report with status `matched`.
2. Every manifest record whose normalised version string does NOT match any billing entry for that package name must appear with status `unmatched`.
3. The canonical hash stored in the database for each ingested record must be the SHA-256 of the UTF-8 bytes of the string `{name}=={normalised_version}` (with exactly two equals signs and no extra whitespace).
4. The reconciliation report's summary line must state correct integer counts of matched, unmatched, and total records — and those counts must be consistent with the detail rows.
5. On any manifest that contains package entries where the version field uses a build-metadata suffix (e.g. `1.2.3+build.7`), the normalised version used for matching and hashing must strip the build-metadata portion (everything after and including the `+`), but must retain pre-release labels (e.g. `1.2.3-alpha.1` stays `1.2.3-alpha.1`).

Verification will run the pipeline against several client manifests that differ from the sample. Produce a fixed pipeline; do not hard-code answers for specific inputs.
requirements: Matched status assigned iff normalised version equals vendor billing entry for that package name
Unmatched status assigned when no billing entry matches normalised version for the package name
Canonical hash = SHA-256 of UTF-8 bytes of '{name}=={normalised_version}' with exactly two equals signs
Summary counts (matched, unmatched, total) are correct integers consistent with detail rows
Build-metadata suffix (after '+') stripped during normalisation; pre-release labels preserved
environment: Dockerfile FROM python:3.13-slim-bookworm; apt-get install sqlite3; pip install click pydantic
/app/reconciler/__init__.py, __main__.py, ingest.py, normalise.py, hash_util.py, db.py, engine.py, report.py — ~1400 lines total

ingest.py: reads JSON manifest, calls normalise.version(), calls hash_util.canonical_hash(), inserts into SQLite; BUG A (data-dependent, not statically obvious): normalise.version() strips the pre-release label instead of the build-metadata suffix — it splits on '-' rather than '+', so '1.2.3+build.7' becomes '1.2.3+build.7' (unchanged, wrong), and '1.2.3-alpha.1' becomes '1.2.3' (stripped, wrong) — this bug only manifests on version strings that contain these patterns

hash_util.py: canonical_hash() computes SHA-256 of '{name}={normalised_version}' (ONE equals sign) rather than two — hash stored in DB is wrong, but sample manifest has no billing entry that checks the hash directly so the sample run appears fine

engine.py: reconciliation JOIN uses the stored hash column to match rather than (name, normalised_version) columns directly — so when hash_util is wrong, matches silently fail even if name+version match; fixing only the normalise bug leaves the hash-join broken; fixing only the hash bug without fixing normalise leaves version matching wrong
report.py: summary count query has a subtle GROUP BY that double-counts packages appearing twice in a manifest (duplicates within one manifest) — only triggers when a manifest has dup package names
db.py: schema migration logic skips adding the normalised_version column if the DB file already exists from a prior run — causes schema errors on re-runs until solver deletes or migrates the DB

/app/data/sample_manifest.json: 8 packages, no build-metadata versions, no pre-release versions, no duplicate names — sample run silently produces wrong hashes but they happen to all be 'unmatched' so counts look plausible
/app/data/vendor_billing.csv: 20 rows of (name, normalised_version, unit_price) loaded by ingest into billing table
/app/tests/: a handful of unit tests that pass even with the bugs (they mock the hash function)
Verification script generates fresh manifests with build-metadata versions, pre-release versions, duplicates, and checks all five requirements against actual pipeline output
blueprint.internal_hint: Difficulty comes from two interacting causes that are NOT visible by static reading of any single file, plus one edge-case correctness requirement on version normalisation that the sample data never exercises. (1) BUG A — normalise.py splits version on the wrong separator ('-' instead of '+') for build-metadata stripping; this is data-dependent: the sample manifest has no such version strings so the bug never fires on sample data. (2) BUG B — engine.py's reconciliation JOIN uses the hash column, not (name, normalised_version); the hash is computed with one '=' in hash_util.py; fixing BUG A alone changes normalised versions but the JOIN still uses the wrong hashes so nothing matches. Fixing BUG B alone (switching the JOIN to name+normalised_version) makes the sample pass but hides BUG A until build-metadata versions appear. The solver must run the pipeline on non-sample data (or construct a test case) to observe the failure, then trace whether the failure is in normalisation, hashing, or matching — three separate modules. BUG C (db.py schema migration skip) forces the solver to deal with a stale DB if they run/re-run without cleaning, which surfaces organically during investigation. BUG D (report.py double-count on duplicates) is a fourth, weaker bug that only shows on duplicate package names. The fixes are: normalise.py: split on '+' and take index 0 for build-metadata, but only do so — leave '-' alone; hash_util.py: use '==' separator; engine.py: JOIN on (name, normalised_version) not hash; report.py: deduplicate or use DISTINCT; db.py: run ALTER TABLE or DROP+recreate on schema mismatch.
blueprint.trap: A solver that fixes only the normalise.py separator bug sees that build-metadata versions now strip correctly, but the engine still joins on the hash, and the hashes are still wrong (one '=' vs two), so reconciliation still fails on non-sample data. A solver that fixes only the hash to use '==' sees sample data pass because the JOIN now computes correct hashes for the sample's simple versions, but build-metadata versions still normalise incorrectly. Both partial fixes produce a pipeline that passes the sample and plausibly looks done, but fails the hidden manifests. The solver must discover and fix all interacting components.
tests: Generate a manifest with 5 packages having plain versions matching billing entries → all 5 must be `matched`, summary total=5 matched=5 unmatched=0

Generate a manifest with 3 packages where version has build-metadata suffix (e.g. '2.1.0+nightly.42') that matches billing entry '2.1.0' after stripping → must appear as `matched`; if suffix not stripped correctly they appear as `unmatched` → test fails
Generate a manifest with 2 packages with pre-release label (e.g. '3.0.0-beta.2') where billing has '3.0.0-beta.2' exactly → must appear as `matched` (pre-release label must NOT be stripped)
Generate a manifest where one package has no billing entry at all → must appear as `unmatched`
Generate a manifest with a duplicate package name (same name, two entries) → summary total must equal number of manifest entries, not double-count
Verify the canonical hash stored in DB for an ingested record equals SHA-256('{name}=={normalised_version}'.encode('utf-8')) by querying the SQLite DB directly after ingest
Run the pipeline twice on the same manifest (simulating re-runs) without manual DB cleanup → must succeed without schema errors on the second run
Generate a manifest with mix of all version types (plain, build-metadata, pre-release, unmatched) → all status assignments and summary counts must be simultaneously correct

verifier_knob.name: fraction_build_metadata_versions
verifier_knob.effect: Increasing the fraction of build-metadata version strings in hidden test manifests makes BUG A more likely to surface and harder to miss; decreasing it makes the task easier because plain-version manifests may pass even with the normalise bug

expected_failure_modes: Solver fixes only normalise.py, verifies on sample, ships — hidden tests with build-metadata versions fail because engine still joins on wrong hash
Solver fixes only hash_util.py separator, verifies on sample, ships — normalisation is still wrong for build-metadata versions

Solver fixes normalise.py and hash_util.py but misses that engine.py joins on hash column — name+version match still broken because hash JOIN computes new correct hashes but old DB rows have old hashes
Solver fixes all three core bugs but misses report.py double-count — tests with duplicate package names produce wrong summary counts
Solver fixes everything but doesn't handle db.py schema migration — second run of the verifier fails with a schema error

speedrun: Edit normalise.py: split version on '+', take [0], leave '-' alone
Edit hash_util.py: change format string from '{name}={v}' to '{name}=={v}'
Edit engine.py: change reconciliation JOIN from hash column to (name, normalised_version) columns
Edit report.py: fix GROUP BY / add DISTINCT to prevent double-counting duplicate package names
Edit db.py: add ALTER TABLE or DROP+recreate logic when normalised_version column missing
Create /tmp/test_build_meta.json with package version '2.1.0+nightly.42', billing has '2.1.0'
Create /tmp/test_dup.json with duplicate package name, run and check summary counts
python -m reconciler run --manifest /tmp/test_dup.json (second run, no DB cleanup) — check no schema error
sqlite3 /app/data/reconciler.db 'SELECT name, hash FROM records' — verify SHA-256 of 'name==normalised_version'
invalid_failure_risks: The 're-run without DB cleanup' test assumes the verifier does NOT reset the container/filesystem between runs; if the verifier uses a fresh container per test, this test is impossible to fail/pass correctly and may be vacuously satisfied or broken.

metric_threshold verifier with fraction_build_metadata_versions=0.4 implies partial credit scoring, but the individual test pass/fail logic is not specified — a solver fixing 4/5 bugs might pass the threshold and be incorrectly accepted.
db.py schema migration bug interacts with verifier ordering: if verifier always starts with a fresh DB, the migration bug never surfaces, making that test case vacuous.

The instruction says 'do not hard-code answers for specific inputs' but the verifier generates manifests at verify-time; if verifier logic leaks package names/versions (e.g., via predictable names), a solver could theoretically target them, though this is unlikely in practice.

All five bugs are independently and statically visible by reading the five relevant source files sequentially; the 'interacting causes' framing overstates the difficulty for a methodical agent, making genuine_difficulty lower than intended.
review.reasons: The task fails the genuine_difficulty threshold: all five bugs are statically visible by reading five source files sequentially (~5 reads + 5 edits + ~10 verification commands = ~20 commands), meaning a frontier agent doing systematic file review will find and fix everything without needing to run the pipeline on non-sample data to discover hidden failures. The 'interacting causes' trap only catches agents that skip reading engine.py, not methodical ones. Additionally, the re-run/schema-migration test has an invalid failure risk: if the verifier resets the container between test cases (common practice), the test is vacuously satisfied and the db.py bug goes undetected.
fixes: To raise genuine_difficulty: obfuscate the bug locations by spreading logic across more files, or make the engine.py JOIN syntactically plausible (e.g., join on a computed expression that looks correct but isn't), so static reading doesn't immediately flag it — force the solver to run and observe failures.

To fix the re-run test: explicitly specify in the environment setup that the verifier runs all tests in a single container session with a shared DB directory, and document this in the instruction so the test is not vacuous.

To improve the metric_threshold verifier: define explicit pass/fail thresholds per test case (e.g., 'all 8 sub-tests must pass') rather than a single fraction knob, to prevent partial fixes from accidentally crossing the threshold.

Consider reducing the number of bugs from 5 to 3 (the three core interacting ones: normalise, hash, engine) and make the interaction harder to spot statically — e.g., the hash_util bug could be in a lambda buried in a larger expression, or engine.py could use a CTE that obscures the join column selection.
